# Sound It Out

> Sound It Out helps parents whose child is stuck in reading (ages 3 to 7: preschool, kindergarten and first grade). Free tools show where to start and point to what may be causing the difficulty. 10-day plans teach one difficulty each, with printable pages, a short video for each day and sound tracks for the child ($19, one payment, 30-day money back). Single printable packs are free to download. Bundles cost $3 or $5.

## Start here
- [Find your child’s reading level](https://sounditoutreading.com/#start): a free level finder with a plan for the week
- [My child is behind in reading: where do I start?](https://sounditoutreading.com/my-child-is-behind-in-reading/): a free finder that points to what may be causing the difficulty
- [Free 3-minute check: Hearing the sounds in words](https://sounditoutreading.com/why-cant-my-child-hear-the-sounds-in-words/)
- [Free 3-minute check: The letter sounds](https://sounditoutreading.com/why-cant-my-child-remember-letter-sounds/)
- [Free 3-minute check: Putting sounds together](https://sounditoutreading.com/why-cant-my-child-blend-sounds/)
- [Free 3-minute check: Guessing at words](https://sounditoutreading.com/why-does-my-child-guess-words-when-reading/)
- [Free 3-minute check: Mixing up b and d](https://sounditoutreading.com/why-does-my-child-mix-up-b-and-d/)
- [Free 3-minute check: Common words that will not stay](https://sounditoutreading.com/why-cant-my-child-remember-sight-words/)
- [Free 3-minute check: Slow, word-by-word reading](https://sounditoutreading.com/why-does-my-child-read-so-slowly/)

## 10-day plans
- [Ears First](https://sounditoutreading.com/ears-first-10-day-listening-plan/): Cannot tell me the first sound of a word, or cannot rhyme. The goal: on day 10 your child hears the sounds in a short word. They say how it starts, push three sounds together into a word, and pull a word apart into its sounds.
- [Eight Sounds That Stay](https://sounditoutreading.com/eight-sounds-that-stay-10-day-plan/): Does not know the letter sounds, or learns them and forgets them. The goal: on day 10 your child says the sound of eight letters, in any order, a day after the last lesson, and uses them to read short words never seen before.
- [From Sounds to Words](https://sounditoutreading.com/from-sounds-to-words-blending-plan/): Knows the sounds, but cannot put them together into a word. The goal: on day 10 your child reads words they have never seen before.
- [Look at Every Letter](https://sounditoutreading.com/look-at-every-letter-10-day-plan/): Guesses words from the first letter or the picture, or “reads” books from memory. The goal: on day 10 your child looks at every letter before saying a word, and reads words and sentences never seen before, with no picture to help.
- [Tell b from d](https://sounditoutreading.com/tell-b-from-d-10-day-plan/): Mixes up b and d. The goal: on day 10 your child tells b from d, in letters, in words never seen before, and in their own writing.
- [Words That Stick](https://sounditoutreading.com/words-that-stick-sight-words-10-day-plan/): Cannot remember common words like the, said and was. The goal: on day 10 your child reads 16 of the most common words, on their own and inside sentences never seen before.
- [Smooth Reading](https://sounditoutreading.com/smooth-reading-10-day-plan/): Reads slowly, one word at a time, or sounds out every word. The goal: on day 10 your child reads a short sentence they have never seen, smoothly, the way they would say it.
- [Read It, See It](https://sounditoutreading.com/read-it-see-it-10-day-plan/): Reads the words but cannot tell me what it said. The goal: on day 10 your child reads a short story they have never seen, tells you what happened, and draws it.
- [Hear It, Write It](https://sounditoutreading.com/hear-it-write-it-10-day-spelling-plan/): Can read simple words but cannot spell them. The goal: on day 10 your child writes short words they have never practiced, every sound in the right order, and reads each one back to check it.
- [Start at the Top](https://sounditoutreading.com/start-at-the-top-10-day-handwriting-plan/): Letters are messy, start in the wrong place or face the wrong way. The goal: on day 10 your child starts every small letter in the right place, sits it on the line, and writes new words that you can read.

- [What Works in Teaching Reading? What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-what-works-in-teaching-reading/): research summary. Two large U.S. reviews point the same way. Here is what they found and how strong the evidence is. Every finding names its source.
- [Does Phonics Work? What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-does-phonics-work/): research summary. Eighteen studies met the standards of a U.S. review. Here is what they showed, and what they did not test. Every finding names its source.
- [Hearing Sounds in Words: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-hearing-the-sounds-in-words/): research summary. Seventeen studies met the standards of a U.S. review, and all seventeen found positive effects. Every finding names its source.
- [Mixing Up b and d: What the Research Guide Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-mixing-up-b-and-d/): research summary. An expert panel says it is common in the early grades, and sets out one letter at a time as the way through. Every finding names its source.
- [Blending Sounds Into Words: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-blending-sounds-into-words/): research summary. An expert panel names this exact problem and sets out what to teach. Every finding names its source.
- [Letter Names or Letter Sounds First? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-letter-names-or-letter-sounds/): research summary. The guide teaches each letter with its sound, a few at a time. Every finding names its source.
- [Sight Words: Memorize or Sound Out? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-sight-words-memorize-or-sound-out/): research summary. Sound out the regular ones. Teach the irregular ones as whole words. Every finding names its source.
- [Guessing Words From Pictures: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-guessing-words-from-pictures/): research summary. A U.S. expert panel discourages guessing, and says why. Every finding names its source.
- [Slow, Word-by-Word Reading: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-slow-reading-and-fluency/): research summary. Reading aloud again and again, with feedback, has the best support. Every finding names its source.
- [Reads the Words but Does Not Understand: The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-reading-comprehension/): research summary. Sounding out is needed but is not enough. Here is what the panel recommends. Every finding names its source.
- [Can Read but Cannot Spell: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-teaching-spelling/): research summary. Breaking a word into its sounds helps children spell, the panel found. Every finding names its source.
- [Handwriting Practice: What the Research Guide Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-handwriting-practice/): research summary. Short practice, letters formed the same way each time, then real writing. Every finding names its source.
- [Reading Aloud to Your Child: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-reading-aloud-to-children/): research summary. It builds spoken language and knowledge of print. It is not the same as teaching the code. Every finding names its source.
- [Talking, Vocabulary and Reading: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-vocabulary-and-talking/): research summary. The guide says the language of books usually has to be taught. The evidence is rated minimal. Every finding names its source.
- [Decodable Books for Beginners: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-decodable-books/): research summary. A good case for decodable books at the very start. Not forever. Every finding names its source.
- [Do Children Learn to Read Naturally? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-do-children-learn-to-read-naturally/): research summary. A major review says the idea that letters stand for sounds has to be taught to most children. Every finding names its source.
- [Dyslexia: Early Signs and What Helps, From Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-dyslexia-early-signs/): research summary. Two research reviews on the signs, the risk factors and the teaching that has support. Every finding names its source.
- [How Often Should a Child Practice Reading? Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-how-often-to-practice-reading/): research summary. Studies used short, regular sessions. A direct test of short against long was not found. Every finding names its source.
- [Does Rhyming Matter for Reading? What Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-does-rhyming-matter/): research summary. Rhyme is an easier first step. The teaching that helped reading most worked on single sounds. Every finding names its source.
- [Reading Longer Words: What the Research Guide Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-reading-longer-words/): research summary. The guide gives a routine: find the parts you know, say them, say them fast, check. Every finding names its source.
- [An Older Child Still Learning to Read: The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-older-child-still-a-beginner/): research summary. Phonics still helped older struggling readers. So did reading aloud again and again. Every finding names its source.
- [Does Reading Tutoring Help? What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-reading-tutoring/): research summary. Extra teaching in small groups has strong support for decoding. Every finding names its source.
- [Sound Games With or Without Letters? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-sound-games-with-letters/): research summary. Sound work done with letters had bigger effects on reading. Every finding names its source.
- [What Parents Can Do at Home: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-what-parents-can-do-at-home/): research summary. In a review of 14 studies, parents teaching specific skills had the largest effect. Every finding names its source.
- [Do Reading Apps Help Young Children? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-reading-apps/): research summary. A positive average effect, with large differences from app to app. Every finding names its source.
- [Learning to Read in a Second Language: The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-english-as-a-second-language/): research summary. The guide reports English learners learning to read at the same rate in K to 2. Every finding names its source.
- [When to Worry About Reading: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-when-to-worry-about-reading/): research summary. The sources name risk signs and school screening. None gives an age to worry. Every finding names its source.
- [Does Being Read To Predict Reading? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-being-read-to-and-later-reading/): research summary. Shared reading helps language. Its effect on reading skills is less sure. Every finding names its source.
- [Early Signs of a Future Reader: What Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-early-predictors-of-reading/): research summary. Letter knowledge and awareness of sounds are among six early skills with the strongest links. Every finding names its source.
- [Forgetting Letter Sounds: What the Research Guides Say](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-remembering-letter-sounds/): research summary. The guides do not explain the forgetting. They do set out what to do. Every finding names its source.

## Guides
- [My Child Cannot Remember Sight Words: What to Do](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-my-child-cannot-remember-sight-words/): Here is why your child forgets sight words right after learning them, and four simple things to try this week to help it stick.
- [How to Teach a Child to Hold a Pencil](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-pencil-grip/): Learn when children are ready to hold a pencil correctly, the exact tripod grip steps to teach, and activities that build hand strength.
- [My Child Guesses Words Instead of Sounding Out](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-my-child-guesses-words-instead-of-sounding-them-out/): Learn why kids guess at words instead of sounding them out, and get four simple steps, with example words, to build real sounding-out skills.
- [How to Teach a Child to Tell Time](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-a-child-to-tell-time/): Find out when children usually learn to tell time, and get simple steps for teaching whole hours, half hours, and minutes on a clock.
- [My Child Does Not Understand Subtraction: What to Do](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-my-child-does-not-understand-subtraction/): Learn why subtraction confuses many young children, and try simple hands-on activities this week to build real number sense at home.
- [My Child Reads Slowly, One Sound at a Time: What to Do](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-child-reads-slowly-one-sound-at-a-time/): Learn why your child reads one sound at a time instead of smoothly, and simple steps to make reading smoother, with no timing.
- [What Is a Sight Word?](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-what-is-a-sight-word/): Learn what a sight word is, why a few common words do not fully follow the sounds, and simple steps to teach them without guessing.
- [When Should a Child Know All Their Letters?](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-when-should-a-child-know-all-letters/): Learn the typical age range for learning all 26 letters, uppercase and lowercase, and what to do if your child needs more practice.
- [My Child Knows Sounds but Cannot Blend: What to Do](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-my-child-knows-sounds-but-cannot-blend/): Your child knows the letter sounds but cannot blend them into words. Learn why this happens and what to try this week.
- [My Child Mixes Up B and D: What to Do](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-my-child-mixes-up-b-and-d/): Your child’s b and d confusion is common. Learn why it happens, what to try at home this week, and when to tell the teacher.
- [What Age Can a Child Cut Shapes and Glue Accurately](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-cutting-and-gluing-skills-by-age/): Learn the age range when children usually learn to cut simple shapes and glue accurately, and how to help build these skills.
- [When Should a Child Learn to Count to 100?](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-when-do-kids-count-to-100/): Learn when children typically count to 100, and simple ways to help your child master counting by tens and ones at home.
